title: SLO dashboards + alerting for cost-model-service (latency/error rate) with runbook links
author: Rafael Mendes
release_notes: Internal: Adds Grafana dashboard + alert rules for cost-model-service SLOs (availability, p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate), and publishes on-call runbook links from alert annotations.
description:
Context: Cost Model API is now a hard dependency for Console cost breakdown and Optimize what-if sweeps. During canary we saw that timeouts/5xxs can degrade Console pages and create noisy support escalations. This PR adds first-pass SLO dashboards and actionable alerting for cost-model-service (latency + error rate) and wires each alert to an on-call runbook.

What’s in this PR: 1) Grafana dashboard for cost-model-service: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency (overall and by endpoint), error rate split (4xx validation vs 5xx), upstream dependency panels (telemetry read latency + model-catalog lookups), and cache effectiveness (internal memoization hit ratio). 2) Prometheus/Alertmanager rules: p95 latency burn alerts (fast + slow), p99 latency page for sustained impact, 5xx rate burn alert, and a separate “validation spike” warning (to catch schema/clients sending bad inputs without paging). 3) SLO recording rules: standard RED signals + burn-rate style alerts. 4) Runbooks: new runbook for cost-model-service with triage steps, common failure modes (telemetry lag, model-catalog timeouts, version negotiation errors, hot partition/cached key skew), and mitigation playbook (feature-flag disable in Console/Optimize, raise client timeout, fall back to v1, enable request shedding). 5) Alert annotations: each rule includes service, owner, severity, and a runbook_url that points to the runbook in this repo.

Alerting policy notes: - Error-rate alerts page only on 5xx. 4xx spikes are warnings and routed to #eng-platform for investigation (often client-side or rollout/config mistakes). - Latency paging is based on burn-rate (fast: 5m window, slow: 1h window) to reduce noise. - Endpoints are grouped by route (estimate vs explain) but do not label by tenant/model to avoid cardinality blowups.

Dashboards: The dashboard is intended for SRE and platform on-call. It uses standard tags (service=cost-model-service, route, status_class, region, deployment_mode) aligned with existing conventions.

Testing/validation: - Verified locally with promtool and grafana lint. - Validated in staging: alerts fire with synthetic load and link to runbook correctly. - Confirmed queries do not introduce new high-cardinality label joins.

Rollout: Safe to merge; dashboards/alerts are inert until deployed to the monitoring stack (Release Eng will pick this up in the next train). Follow-up: we should tune thresholds after a week of baseline data in prod.

Screenshots: Added to the PR conversation (Grafana panels: latency heatmap, error split, dependency breakdown).

Related: ENG-23217, and follows earlier cost-model-service performance work in the canary threads. (No customer-facing billing changes; purely operational tooling.)
commits: monitoring: add cost-model-service SLO recording rules
alerting: add burn-rate alerts for latency + 5xx rate
runbooks: add cost-model-service oncall runbook and wire alert annotations
chore: fix query label joins and lint issues
conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): The dashboard looks good. Two requests: (1) can we split 4xx into validation vs authz? We’ve had auth issues look like ‘bad requests’ historically. (2) Please add a note in the runbook about Console fallback behavior and the feature flag name to disable SCM calls if we’re paging on latency.

Rafael Mendes (author): Good call. I added status_reason=validation|authz to the error split panel (query uses existing metric label; no new series). Also added a ‘Client impact + mitigations’ section to the runbook with Console fallback and the flags. Flag names included: console.cost_breakdown.use_scm + optimize.scenario_eval.use_scm.

Allison Grant (review): Please remove any grouping by model_id in the dashboard. Even if it’s hidden by default it will tempt people into high-cardinality dashboards. Also, for alerts, we should avoid route+region+deployment_mode all together unless we’ve validated series counts.

Rafael Mendes (author): Done. Dashboard now groups primarily by route and status_class, with region as a dashboard variable (off by default). Alerts are global per service (no region label) to keep noise down; region-specific breakdown is in the dashboard for investigation.
Logan Wright (review): The dependency panels reference telemetry read latency. Can you ensure those metrics exist in all regions? In eu-west we’ve had gaps when the telemetry proxy is unhealthy.

Rafael Mendes (author): Added a dashboard panel that shows missing-series rate for telemetry dependency metrics and a runbook note: ‘If dependency metrics are missing, use service logs + trace sampling and check telemetry proxy health.’

Chloe Martin (review): Thanks for including runbook_url annotations; Console oncall will need those. One thing: can we add an alert annotation indicating ‘customer impact likely’ if p99 is breached for >10m? That’s what our page policy uses for upstream deps.
Neha Kapoor (review): +1. Also, can you set the default severity to page only for 5xx and p99 latency. p95 burn should be a ticket/warn. We’ve been burned by p95 pages for bursty traffic.

Rafael Mendes (author): Updated severities: p99 sustained + 5xx burn are paging; p95 burn is warning (ticket). Added ‘impact_hint’ annotation with suggested customer impact guidance; kept it static to avoid complex logic inside alert rules.
Sean Gallagher (approve): LGTM after latest updates. Queries look standard, no cardinality footguns. Approving.
Allison Grant (approve): Approved. Thanks for moving region/model breakdown out of alert labels.
Neha Kapoor (approve): Approved. Please follow up after a week of prod to tune thresholds based on baseline.
Rafael Mendes (author): Merged (squash). Follow-up task filed in Linear to revisit alert thresholds after baseline week.
